# The book of shares_bought_in_a_transaction_stating_no_canadian_figure.txt,
# with the cost basis the dollars came out of stating its own balance.
#
# `cost_basis_balance: "7800.00"` on the dollars bought is what that cost basis
# holds once the file has landed: 10,000.00 bought, 2,200.00 spent on the
# shares. Every export writes the line, so this is the shape a book takes when
# it is exported and imported again, or when its author writes the balance down.
#
# A stated balance is already net of the purchase, so the purchase does not
# lower it a second time. It still spends 2,200.00 dollars that cost 1.30, and
# that cost goes onto the shares exactly as it does when the balance is not
# stated:
#
#     2,000.00 USD to USD_TECH  ->  2,600.00 CAD  ->  52.00 a share
#       200.00 USD to USD_CORP  ->    260.00 CAD  ->  26.00 a share
#
# The sale then draws on the USD_TECH cost basis, which is there to draw on only
# because the cost was carried.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_a_share_purchase_is_costed_from_a_cost_basis_whose_balance_the_file_states.py.
